mainTopic: Taanit 16a: The reasons behind the fast-day rituals, the rebuke calling for תשובה, and the qualities of the fast-day prayer leader
overview: This amud explains the meaning behind the public fast-day rituals described in the משנה. It opens by finishing the explanation of why others place ashes on the leaders' heads, and רבי יצחק teaches that the ashes go where the head-תפילין sit, based on 'פאר תחת אפר'. A סימן then lists the rituals to be explained, and the גמרא goes through each one: going out to the רחוב, bringing out the תיבה, wearing שקים, ash on the תיבה, ash on each person's head, and going to the cemetery. For several of these, two אמוראים give different reasons, and the גמרא finds the practical difference (מאי בינייהו) between them. Because רבי לוי בר חמא and רבי חנינא disagree twice, the גמרא adds a third dispute of theirs about the meaning of the name הר המוריה. The גמרא then returns to the משנה's speech of rebuke: תשובה and good deeds, not sackcloth and fasting, bring atonement, as seen with the people of נינוה. It explains several פסוקים about נינוה's repentance, and רב אדא בר אהבה compares confessing without leaving the sin to immersing while holding a שרץ. Finally, a ברייתא and רבי יהודה describe the ideal fast-day prayer leader, and the חכמים look to רב יצחק בר אמי as the one who fits.

steps.title: Being shamed by others is stronger than shaming yourself
steps.stepSummary: The tail end of the previous explanation: ashes are put on the leaders' heads by others, because being humiliated by others is not like humiliating yourself.
steps.simpleTranslation: [It is not the same, one who is embarrassed by himself and one who is embarrassed] by others.
steps.whatsHappening: This amud starts in the middle of a sentence. The גמרא is finishing its explanation of why someone else puts the ashes on the head of the נשיא and the אב בית דין, instead of them doing it themselves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full line is 'אינו דומה מתבייש מעצמו למתבייש מאחרים': being humbled by another person is a deeper humiliation than humbling yourself. That is why the משנה has others place the ashes on the leaders' heads.

keyTerms.meaning: One who is embarrassed or humiliated

phrases.english: to one who is embarrassed by others.
phrases.notes: End of the sentence 'It is not the same, one embarrassed by himself, compared to one embarrassed by others.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation begun on the previous section of the daf about why others place the ashes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ashes are placed on the leaders by others, because humiliation from others is greater than self-humiliation.

steps.title: Where on the head are the ashes placed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the exact spot on the head where the ashes are put.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where does one place them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple practical question: where exactly on the head do the ashes go? This sets up רבי יצחק's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said to put ashes 'בראש', on the head, but did not say where on the head. The גמרא now asks for that missing detail.

phrases.english: And where does one place them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from why others place the ashes to where the ashes are placed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The precise location on the head for the ashes.

steps.title: The ashes go where the תפילין are worn
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק says the ashes go on the spot of the head-תפילין, and proves it from a פסוק in ישעיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: On the place of the תפילין, as it says, 'To appoint for the mourners of Zion, to give them a glorious ornament (פאר) instead of ashes (אפר).'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק answers that the ashes are placed where the head-תפילין sit. He brings a פסוק as support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says that in the future, mourners will receive 'פאר instead of אפר'. Elsewhere (יחזקאל 24:17), פאר is understood to mean תפילין. So now, in mourning, the ashes sit exactly where the פאר, the תפילין, would go.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
On the place of the tefillin.
As it is stated: 'To appoint for the mourners of Zion,'
to give them an ornament instead of ashes.'
phrases.notes: פאר (ornament) replaces אפר (ashes), so both occupy the same spot. Note the wordplay: the two words use the same letters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of where the ashes are placed.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: On the spot of the head-tefillin, derived from 'פאר תחת אפר'.
steps.whatToRemember: The fast-day ashes go on the spot of the head-תפילין, because the פסוק contrasts פאר (תפילין) with אפר, so they belong in the same place.

steps.title: A memory list for the upcoming questions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a סימן listing, in order, the topics it is about to explain.
steps.simpleTranslation: Square, ark, sackcloth, ashes, ashes, burial, and Moriah: this is a mnemonic.
steps.whatsHappening: This is not an argument. It is a memory aid listing the next questions the גמרא will ask about the fast-day rituals, so the learner can keep them in order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word is the heading of an upcoming question. רחוב asks why they go to the square. תיבה asks why the ark is taken out. שקים asks why sackcloth is worn. The two אפר words ask about the ashes on the תיבה and on each person's head. קבורה asks why they go to the cemetery. מוריה asks about the name of הר המוריה. Steps 5–27 go through all seven items in this order.

keyTerms.meaning: The ark holding the ספר תורה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't try to read this line as a sentence. It is just a list of headings for what comes next.

phrases.english: Square, ark, and sackcloth, ashes,
ashes, burial, and Moriah: a mnemonic.

steps.triggerLanguage: רְחוֹב, תֵּיבָה, וְשַׂקִּים, אֵפֶר, אֵפֶר, קְבוּרָה, וּמוֹרִיָּה סִימָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section explaining the meaning of each fast-day ritual.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lists the order of the upcoming explanations of the fast-day rituals.

steps.title: Why go out to the town square?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind gathering in the public square on a fast day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do they go out to the square?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the first question from the סימן: what is the point of leaving the בית כנסת and praying in the public square? Two answers follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה describes this practice but gives no reason for it. The גמרא wants the meaning behind the action.

phrases.english: Why do they go out to the square?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first item of the סימן (רחוב).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The symbolic reason for praying in the public square.

steps.title: Public self-humbling after private prayer failed
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא says going out shows: we prayed privately and were not answered, so now we humble ourselves publicly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said: It is to say: We cried out in private and were not answered; we will disgrace ourselves in public.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר אבא gives the first reason. Going outside is a way of saying 'praying quietly didn't work, so now we humiliate ourselves in front of everyone.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: For him, the key is publicity. Taking the prayer from the private בית כנסת into the open increases the humiliation, in the hope that this greater humility brings an answer.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said:
To say: We cried out in private and were not answered;
we will disgrace ourselves in public.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to why they go to the square.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is public self-humiliation after unanswered private prayer.

steps.title: Going out is a form of exile that atones
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says going out symbolizes exile: we have been exiled, and may our exile atone for us.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: We have gone into exile; may our exile atone for us.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives a different reason. Leaving the usual place of prayer acts like a small exile, and exile brings כפרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For ריש לקיש, the key is not publicity but displacement. The act of leaving one's place works like גלות, which atones for sin.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
We have been exiled; may our exile atone for us.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, competing answer to the same question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Going out is a symbolic exile that brings atonement.

steps.title: What is the practical difference between them?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks in what case the two reasons would lead to different results.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the two reasons ever lead to different practical outcomes. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the usual case, going to the square fits both reasons, since it is both public and a displacement. The גמרא wants a case where only one reason applies.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the (practical) difference between them?

phrases.english: What is between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two answers just given.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the two reasons give different results.

steps.title: Moving from one בית כנסת to another
steps.stepSummary: The difference arises if they move from one בית כנסת to another, which counts as exile but is not public.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them where they moved from one synagogue to another synagogue.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two reasons split when the people move from one בית כנסת to another instead of going to the square.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For ריש לקיש, this works, because they left their place, which counts as exile. For רבי חייא בר אבא, it does not work, because a בית כנסת is still private, so there is no public humiliation.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them

steps.whatToRemember: רבי חייא בר אבא focuses on public humiliation, and ריש לקיש focuses on exile. Moving from one בית כנסת to another satisfies only ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them:
where they were exiled from one synagogue to another synagogue.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ דְּגָלוּ מִבֵּי כְנִישְׁתָּא לְבֵי כְנִישְׁתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מאי בינייהו question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Moving from one synagogue to another is sufficient for ריש לקיש (exile) but not for רבי חייא בר אבא (no public disgrace).

steps.title: Why bring the תיבה out to the square?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the second question from the סימן: why take the ark out to the town square.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why do they take the ark out to the town square?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second item on the list, the תיבה, and asks why it is carried into the public square. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה requires the תיבה to be brought out, but does not say why. This is a separate ritual from the people themselves going out, so it needs its own reason.

phrases.english: And why do they bring out the ark
to the town square?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָמָּה מוֹצִיאִין אֶת הַתֵּיבָה לִרְחוֹבָהּ שֶׁל עִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next item of the סימן (תיבה).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The symbolic reason for bringing the ark into the square.

steps.title: Our modest holy object has been exposed
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי says it shows that our modest, hidden vessel has been disgraced because of our sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: To say: We had a modest vessel, and it has been disgraced because of our sins.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי explains that taking the תיבה outside is a sign of sorrow. Something holy that is normally kept private is now exposed in public, and we admit it is our fault.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תיבה is normally kept modestly inside the בית כנסת. Exposing it in the street is a deliberate act of disgrace that expresses how far we have fallen because of our עוונות.
steps.whatToRemember: Each fast-day ritual has a meaning. Going out to the square is either public humbling or symbolic exile, and bringing out the תיבה shows that a hidden holy object has been exposed because of our sins.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי, לוֹמַר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: To say:
We had a modest vessel,
and it has been disgraced because of our sins.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי לוֹמַר כְּלִי צָנוּעַ הָיָה לָנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers why the ark is brought out.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It expresses that a modest holy vessel has been publicly disgraced because of our sins.

steps.title: Why do they wear sackcloth?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind covering oneself in שק on a public fast.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why do they cover themselves in sackcloth?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next fast-day ritual and asks why people wear שק. It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the same pattern as the earlier questions about the תיבה. The גמרא is not asking whether to do this. It only wants the meaning behind a practice already known from the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: sackcloth, a rough garment worn in mourning or distress

phrases.english: And why do they cover themselves in sackcloth?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next question in the series about the reasons for the fast-day rituals
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The symbolic meaning of wearing שק

steps.title: We are like animals
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא explains that sackcloth expresses that we are worth no more than animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said: It is to say, 'We are considered like animals.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר אבא answers that wearing שק is a way of saying, 'We are like animals before You.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sackcloth is often made from animal hair, and animals are covered in hide. By wearing it, the people lower themselves and admit they have no merit of their own.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said:
To say: we are considered like animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about sackcloth
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Sackcloth expresses that we are considered like animals

steps.title: Why put ashes on the ark?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why burnt ash is placed on top of the תיבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why do they place burnt ashes on top of the ark?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about another ritual: putting burnt ash on the תיבה, the ark holding the ספר תורה. It is setting up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא explained why the תיבה is brought out to the town square. Now it asks why ash is put specifically on the תיבה itself.

keyTerms.meaning: burnt ash, ash left from burning
the ark that holds the ספר תורה

phrases.english: And why do they place burnt ashes
on top of the ark?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָמָּה נוֹתְנִין אֵפֶר מִקְלֶה עַל גַּבֵּי תֵּיבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New question about a different ritual
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of putting ash on the תיבה

steps.title: ה׳ is with us in our trouble
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בן פזי says the ash on the תיבה expresses the פסוק 'I am with him in trouble.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בן פזי said: It is as if to say, 'I am with him in trouble.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה בן פזי answers that ash on the תיבה shows ה׳ is, so to speak, suffering together with us, as the פסוק in תהלים says.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תיבה represents the שכינה‎, ה׳'s Presence. Ash on people shows their own pain. Ash on the תיבה shows that ה׳ shares that pain.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I am with him in trouble' (תהלים צא:טו)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Pazi said:
As if to say: 'I am with him in trouble.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about ash on the תיבה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It shows that ה׳ shares in Israel's suffering, based on 'עמו אנכי בצרה'

steps.title: Another verse with the same idea
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש brings a different פסוק: 'In all their affliction, He was afflicted.'
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: 'In all their affliction, He was afflicted.'
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives the same basic idea but grounds it in a different פסוק, from ישעיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no real argument about the reason. Both agree the ash shows ה׳ shares our pain. ריש לקיש just cites another source for it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'In all their affliction, He was afflicted' (ישעיה סג:ט)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as an argument with רבי יהודה בן פזי. The idea is the same; only the פסוק is different.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
'In all their affliction, He was afflicted.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a parallel source for the same answer
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Same idea, based on 'בכל צרתם לו צר'

steps.title: רבי זירא's trembling
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says that when he saw the Rabbis put ash on the תיבה, his whole body would shake.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: At first, when I would see the Rabbis placing burnt ashes on top of the ark, my whole body would tremble.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא shares a personal reaction. Seeing ash placed on the תיבה moved him so deeply that his whole body shook.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds no new law. It shows how powerful the ritual is once you understand that it means ה׳ Himself is in pain with us.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:

phrases.aramaic: מֵרֵישׁ כִּי הֲוָה חֲזֵינָא לְהוּ לְרַבָּנַן
phrases.english: At first, when I would see the Rabbis

phrases.aramaic: דְּיָהֲבִי אֵפֶר מִקְלֶה עַל גַּבֵּי תֵּיבָה —
phrases.english: placing burnt ashes on top of the ark,
my whole body would tremble.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Personal testimony about the ritual just explained
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ash on the תיבה is a deeply moving sight that made רבי זירא tremble

steps.title: Why put ashes on each person's head?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why ash is placed on the head of every single person.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why do they place ashes on the head of each and every one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next ritual: ash on each individual's head. It is setting up a disagreement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ash on the תיבה was explained as ה׳ sharing our pain. Ash on each person needs its own explanation.

phrases.english: And why do they place ashes
on the head of each and every one?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָמָּה נוֹתְנִין אֵפֶר בְּרֹאשׁ כׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New question about a different ritual
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of ash on each person's head

steps.title: Two reasons: humility, or יצחק's ashes
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי בר חמא and רבי חנינא disagree. One says we are like ash before ה׳; the other says it reminds ה׳ of the ashes of יצחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי לוי בר חמא and רבי חנינא disagree about this. One said: We are considered like ash before You. And one said: So that He will remember for us the ashes of יצחק.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give different reasons for the ash on each head. One says it shows we are like ash, and the other says it reminds ה׳ of the עקידה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first reason is about our humility: we admit we are nothing. The second is about זכות אבות: the ash recalls יצחק, who was ready to be sacrificed, so that ה׳ will remember that merit for us.

keyTerms.meaning: the ashes of יצחק, from the עקידה

phrases.aramaic: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי לֵוִי בַּר חָמָא וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא.
phrases.english: Rabbi Levi bar Chama and Rabbi Chanina disagree about it.

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר: הֲרֵי אָנוּ חֲשׁוּבִין לְפָנֶיךָ כְּאֵפֶר,
phrases.english: One said: we are considered before You like ash,
and one said: so that He will remember for us
the ashes of Yitzchak.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי לֵוִי בַּר חָמָא וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question with two opinions
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either humility (we are like ash) or recalling the merit of יצחק's ashes

steps.title: What is the practical difference?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the two reasons for the ash.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the two reasons would ever lead to a different practice. It is setting up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same move the גמרא made earlier about going out to the town square (steps 8–9). When there are two reasons, it looks for a case where they lead to different results.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the difference between them (in practice)?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical result of the disagreement
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the two reasons give different results

steps.title: The difference: plain earth
steps.stepSummary: The difference is whether plain earth can be used instead of ash.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is plain earth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two reasons differ when someone uses ordinary earth instead of ash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the point is humility, earth works just as well, because it also shows we are lowly. If the point is to recall יצחק's ashes, earth does not work, because only ash connects to the עקידה.

keyTerms.meaning: there is a difference between them

steps.whatToRemember: Ash on the head is either for humility, so earth also works, or for יצחק's merit, so only ash works.

phrases.english: The difference between them is plain earth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מאי בינייהו question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Plain earth: valid for the humility reason, not valid for the יצחק reason

steps.title: Why go to the cemetery?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why people go out to the בית הקברות on a fast day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do they go out to the cemetery?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about another fast-day custom: visiting the cemetery. It is setting up another disagreement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as the ash question. First comes the question, then two opinions, then the practical difference.

phrases.english: Why do they go out to the cemetery?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New question about a different practice
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for visiting the cemetery on a fast day

steps.title: Two reasons: we are like the dead, or the dead pray for us
steps.stepSummary: The same two אמוראים disagree. One says it shows we are like the dead; the other says it is so the dead will ask for mercy for us.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי לוי בר חמא and רבי חנינא disagree about this. One said: We are considered before You like the dead. And one said: So that the dead will ask for mercy on our behalf.
steps.whatsHappening: Again two reasons are given. One is about our own humility, and the other is about getting help from the dead, who pray for us.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches the pattern of the ash dispute. One reason is humility, comparing ourselves to the dead. The other looks for outside help, from the righteous dead who plead for us.

phrases.aramaic: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי לֵוִי בַּר חָמָא וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא.
phrases.english: Rabbi Levi bar Chama and Rabbi Chanina disagree about it.

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר: הֲרֵי אָנוּ חֲשׁוּבִין לְפָנֶיךָ כְּמֵתִים,
phrases.english: One said: we are considered before You like the dead,
and one said: so that they will ask on our behalf,
the dead, for mercy.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי לֵוִי בַּר חָמָא וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the cemetery question with two opinions
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either humility (we are like the dead) or so the dead will pray for us

steps.title: What is the practical difference here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא again asks what practical difference the two reasons make.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same מאי בינייהו question, this time about the cemetery reasons. It is setting up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants a case where only one of the two reasons applies.

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical result of the cemetery dispute
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the two cemetery reasons give different results

steps.title: The difference: graves of non-Jews
steps.stepSummary: The difference is whether going to non-Jewish graves is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is graves of non-Jews.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the reasons differ for a cemetery of non-Jews.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the point is 'we are like the dead,' any graves work, including those of non-Jews. If the point is for the dead to pray for us, it must be Jewish graves, since non-Jews would not plead for Israel.
steps.whatToRemember: Cemetery visits are either for humility, so any graves work, or for the dead to pray for us, so only Jewish graves work.

phrases.english: The difference between them is graves of non-Jews.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מאי בינייהו question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Non-Jewish graves: valid for the humility reason, not for the reason of the dead praying for us

steps.title: What does the name הר המוריה mean?
steps.stepSummary: Since it is quoting רבי לוי בר חמא and רבי חנינא, the גמרא brings another dispute of theirs: the meaning of the name הר המוריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is הר המוריה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a related topic. Because these two אמוראים argued twice already, it brings a third argument of theirs, about the name of the Temple Mount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not about fast-day practice. It is linked by the same pair of disputants. The question concerns the meaning behind the name 'מוריה.'
steps.confusionAlert: This is a side topic brought in because the same two אמוראים argue about it. It is not another fast-day ritual.

phrases.english: What is Mount Moriah?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Related side topic brought because of the same disputants
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the name מוריה

steps.title: Instruction for Israel, or fear for the nations
steps.stepSummary: One says מוריה comes from הוראה, since teaching went out from there to Israel. The other says it comes from מורא, since fear went out from there to the nations.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי לוי בר חמא and רבי חנינא disagree about this. One said: The mountain from which instruction went out to Israel. And one said: The mountain from which fear went out to the nations of the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The two אמוראים read the name 'מוריה' as a play on two different words. One reads it as teaching for Israel, and the other as awe for the nations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first reading points to the סנהדרין גדולה, which sat on the Temple Mount and taught the law to all Israel. The second points to the awe the nations felt toward the place of ה׳'s Presence and His chosen people.
steps.whatToRemember: מוריה means either הוראה (teaching for Israel) or מורא (awe for the nations).

phrases.aramaic: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי לֵוִי בַּר חָמָא וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא.
phrases.english: Rabbi Levi bar Chama and Rabbi Chanina disagree about it.
One said: the mountain from which went out
instruction to Israel,
and one said: the mountain from which went out
fear to the nations of the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי לֵוִי בַּר חָמָא וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the name מוריה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מוריה comes either from הוראה (instruction for Israel) or from מורא (fear for the nations)

steps.title: The eldest gives words of rebuke
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: on a fast day, the eldest person speaks words of rebuke to the people.
steps.simpleTranslation: The eldest among them says words of rebuke in front of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes the next line, about who gives the rebuke on a public fast day. This quote sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the גמרא was explaining the reasons for the fast-day rituals and then went off to the side topic of the name הר המוריה. Now it goes back to the משנה and a new part of the fast-day ceremony: the speech that pushes people toward תשובה.

keyTerms.meaning: Words of rebuke that 'press' the heart toward תשובה

phrases.english: The eldest among them
says before them words of rebuke.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַזָּקֵן שֶׁבָּהֶן אוֹמֵר לִפְנֵיהֶן דִּבְרֵי כִבּוּשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the aggadic tangent about הר המוריה to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On a public fast day, the eldest person speaks words of rebuke to the people.

steps.title: A ברייתא gives an order of who should speak
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא sets the order: a זקן speaks first. If there is none, a חכם speaks. If there is no חכם, an אדם של צורה speaks.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: If there is a זקן, the זקן speaks. If not, a חכם speaks. If not, an אדם של צורה (a person of dignified appearance) speaks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that adds detail to the משנה by ranking who should give the rebuke.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only named the זקן. The ברייתא adds backup choices for a place that has no זקן.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Rabbis taught'; this introduces a ברייתא
A person of dignified, impressive appearance

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
If there is an elder, the elder says it.
And if not, a Sage says it.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לָאו — אוֹמֵר אָדָם שֶׁל צוּרָה.
phrases.english: And if not, a person of dignified appearance says it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אִם יֵשׁ זָקֵן אוֹמֵר זָקֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the משנה's rule with an order of preference.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The order of speakers is: זקן, then חכם, then אדם של צורה.

steps.title: Does an unlearned elder come before a scholar?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: does the ברייתא really mean an old man who is not learned should speak before a חכם?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that to say the elder we mentioned comes first even though he is not a Sage?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the order in the ברייתא, because it seems to place age above Torah learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain reading puts a זקן ahead of a חכם. That seems wrong, because Torah knowledge should matter more than age alone.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is that to say...?'; it opens a surprised challenge

phrases.english: Is that to say the elder we spoke of comes first,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָאו חָכָם הוּא?
phrases.english: even though he is not a Sage?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ranking in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ranking of זקן above חכם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Age alone should not outrank Torah scholarship.

steps.title: אביי: the elder must also be a scholar
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the ברייתא means a זקן who is also a חכם. If there is none, a younger חכם speaks. If there is no חכם, an אדם של צורה speaks.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said, this is what it means: If there is an elder who is also a Sage, that elder Sage speaks. If not, a Sage speaks. If not, a person of dignified appearance speaks.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by reading the ברייתא more precisely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'זקן' in the ברייתא is not just any old man. He is an older חכם. So learning always comes before age alone, and age only adds extra weight when the person is also learned.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is what it means'; a re-reading of the text

phrases.english: Abaye said: this is what it means:
If there is an elder who is also a Sage,
that elder who is a Sage says it.
And if not, a Sage says it.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לָאו — אוֹמֵר אָדָם שֶׁל צוּרָה.
phrases.english: And if not, a person of dignified appearance says it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קשיא by re-reading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A זקן speaks first even if he is unlearned.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first choice is a זקן who is also a חכם. After him comes any חכם, and after that an אדם של צורה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that Torah learning, not age alone, decides who leads the community.

steps.title: The rebuke: repentance, not sackcloth, brings forgiveness
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's speech begins: 'Our brothers, sackcloth and fasting do not bring atonement. תשובה and good deeds do.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Our brothers, it is not sackcloth and fasting that bring it about. Rather, repentance and good deeds bring it about.
steps.whatsHappening: The text now gives the actual words the speaker says to the people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The outward acts of the fast day, like sackcloth and fasting, are only tools. What God responds to is real תשובה and changed behavior.

keyTerms.meaning: Sackcloth, a rough garment worn in mourning or distress

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the fast is useless. It means the fast only works when it leads to real change.

phrases.english: Our brothers, it is not sackcloth and fasting that bring it about,
but rather repentance and good deeds bring it about.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the content of the rebuke whose speaker was just defined.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Atonement comes through תשובה and good deeds, not through outward signs of mourning alone.

steps.title: Proof from the people of נינוה
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק in יונה does not say God saw their sackcloth and fasting. It says God saw their deeds, that they turned from their evil way.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we find with the people of נינוה: it does not say about them 'And God saw their sackcloth and their fasting,' but rather 'And God saw their deeds, that they turned from their evil way.'
steps.whatsHappening: The speech backs up its main point with a proof from ספר יונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people of נינוה did wear sackcloth and fast. Yet the פסוק describes God responding only to their deeds and to their turning away from evil. That wording shows what actually brought the decree to an end.

keyTerms.meaning: 'For so we find'; it introduces a supporting source

steps.whatToRemember: The key message of the fast-day rebuke: God looks at real change in behavior, not only at outward signs of mourning.

phrases.english: For so we find with the people of Nineveh,
that it is not said about them:
'And God saw their sackcloth and their fasting,'
but rather: 'And God saw their deeds,
that they turned from their evil way.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the claim in the previous step.
steps.raayaObject: That תשובה and good deeds, not sackcloth and fasting, bring atonement

steps.title: What did נינוה do with the animals in sackcloth?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says both people and animals were covered in sackcloth. The גמרא asks what they actually did.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And let them be covered with sackcloth, man and beast.' What did they do?
steps.whatsHappening: Since the topic is now נינוה, the גמרא moves into an aggadic explanation of another פסוק about them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting sackcloth on animals seems strange. The גמרא wants to know what the people of נינוה actually did with the animals, and what they meant by it.

phrases.english: 'And let them be covered with sackcloth, man and beast,'
what did they do?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: An aggadic tangent that grows out of the נינוה proof.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the people of נינוה did with the animals

steps.title: They separated mothers from their young
steps.stepSummary: They separated the mother animals from their young, so the animals cried out. Then they told God: if You have no mercy on us, we will have no mercy on these.
steps.simpleTranslation: They tied up the animals separately and the young separately. They said before Him: Master of the World! If You do not have mercy on us, we will not have mercy on these.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the people of נינוה made the animals cry out and used that crying to ask God for mercy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animals had done nothing wrong. By making the animals suffer and linking them to their own fate, the people pushed for God's mercy: even if we do not deserve it, these innocent creatures do.

phrases.english: They tied up the mother animals by themselves,
and the young by themselves.
They said before Him: Master of the World!
If You do not have mercy on us,
we will not have mercy on these.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They separated the mother animals from their young and made the animals' suffering a plea for mercy.

steps.title: What did they say when they 'cried mightily'?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says they called out to God 'with strength.' The גמרא asks what they said.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And let them call out to God mightily.' What did they say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the next phrase in the same פסוק and asks what their 'strong' prayer contained.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בחזקה suggests a bold, forceful argument, not just a loud cry. The גמרא wants to know the content of that argument.

phrases.english: 'And let them call out to God mightily,'
what did they say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel question on the next phrase of the same פסוק.

steps.title: Who must give way to whom?
steps.stepSummary: They argued: when an insulted person faces one who is not insulted, or a צדיק faces a רשע, who should give in? Surely the righteous one gives in. So God should give in and forgive us.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said before Him: Master of the World! One who is humble and one who is not, a righteous person and a wicked one: who gives way before whom?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the bold argument the people of נינוה made in their prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their claim is that the greater and more righteous side is the one expected to give in. Since God is the צדיק in this conflict, they argued that He should be the one to forgive. That daring argument is why the פסוק calls their prayer 'mighty'.

keyTerms.meaning: One who is insulted or humble and bears it quietly
A righteous person and a wicked person

steps.whatToRemember: The people of נינוה combined real change in behavior with forceful prayer: they used the animals' crying and a bold argument to ask for mercy.

phrases.english: They said before Him: Master of the World!
One who is humble and one who is not humble,
a righteous person and a wicked person:
who gives way before whom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה about their prayer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They argued that the righteous side gives way, so God should forgive them.

steps.title: What does 'the violence in their hands' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next part of the פסוק in יונה and asks what 'the violence that is in their hands' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And let them turn, each one from his evil way, and from the violence that is in their hands.' What does 'and from the violence that is in their hands' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps reading the פסוקים about נינוה. Now it asks about one phrase: what was the 'violence in their hands' that they gave up?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא already showed that God looked at what the people of נינוה did, not only at their fasting. Now it wants to know exactly what they did about 'violence in their hands.' This question sets up שמואל's answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Violence or robbery; taking what belongs to someone else
What is / what does it mean

phrases.english: "And let them turn, each one from his evil way
phrases.notes: יונה 3:8, the king of נינוה's announcement

phrases.english: and from the violence that is in their hands."
What is meant by "and from the violence that is in their hands"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the line-by-line reading of the פסוקים in יונה, moving to the next phrase.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What concrete act is meant by turning away from 'the violence in their hands'?

steps.title: They tore down whole buildings to return one stolen beam
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that even someone who stole a beam and built it into a large building would tear the whole building down to give the beam back.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: Even if someone stole a beam and built it into a large building, he would tear down the entire building and give the beam back to its owner.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the question. The people of נינוה gave back stolen property completely, even when it cost them a whole building.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מריש is a wooden beam. A בירה is a large building. Tearing down a whole building for one beam is very costly. This shows their תשובה was complete: they did not keep any stolen thing, even if giving it back hurt them badly.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not the regular הלכה. The חכמים made a rule (תקנת השבים) that a thief who built a stolen beam into a building only pays its value in money, so that people are not scared away from doing תשובה. The people of נינוה went beyond the rule to fully clean themselves of stolen property.

phrases.english: Shmuel said: Even if one stole a beam
and built it into a large building,
he tears down the entire building, all of it,
and returns the beam to its owner.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: אֲפִילּוּ גָּזַל מָרִישׁ וּבְנָאוֹ בְּבִירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 38.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Violence in their hands' means stolen property. They gave it back fully, even tearing down a building to return one stolen beam.

steps.title: Confessing without stopping is like immersing while holding a שרץ
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה compares someone who confesses a sin but keeps doing it to a person who goes to the מקוה while still holding a שרץ. The טבילה does not work until he throws the שרץ away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: A person who has a sin, and he confesses but does not stop doing it, what is he like? He is like a person holding a שרץ (a dead creeping animal that makes people טמא) in his hand. Even if he immerses in all the waters of the world, his טבילה does not work. But once he throws it away and immerses in a מקוה of forty סאה, his טבילה works right away.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה gives a new teaching with a parable. Saying sorry while still holding on to the sin does not help, just like a טבילה does not help while you still hold the thing that makes you טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits the story of נינוה: real תשובה means letting go of the sin, like they let go of the stolen beam. In the parable, the water is not the problem. The שרץ in his hand keeps making him טמא again. Once he lets go, even a regular-size מקוה of forty סאה works immediately.

keyTerms.meaning: Confesses (says out loud that he sinned)
Turns back from it, stops doing the sin
A dead creeping animal that makes a person טמא when touched
Immersion in a מקוה to become טהור
Forty סאה, the minimum amount of water for a kosher מקוה
It worked for him, it counted

steps.whatToRemember: וידוי (confession) only works when it comes with really leaving the sin. Words without change are like immersing while holding a שרץ.

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
A person who has a sin in his hand,
and he confesses but does not turn back from it,
what is he like?
Like a person who holds a dead creeping animal in his hand,
who, even if he immerses in all the waters of the world,
the immersion does not work for him.
Once he throws it from his hand,
as soon as he immerses in forty se'a,
the immersion works for him immediately,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: אָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּיָדוֹ עֲבֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A related new teaching. It expands the lesson of נינוה, that real תשובה means fully letting go of the sin.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Confession without leaving the sin does not work. Once the sin is left behind, תשובה works right away.

steps.title: פסוקים showing that confession must come with leaving the sin
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה supports his teaching with two פסוקים: 'Whoever confesses and leaves it will get mercy' and 'Let us lift our hearts with our hands to God in heaven.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'Whoever confesses and leaves [his sins] will get mercy.' And it also says: 'Let us lift up our heart with our hands to God in heaven.'
steps.whatsHappening: This step brings proof from פסוקים for the parable of the שרץ. Both פסוקים show that words or gestures alone are not enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק (משלי) gives mercy only to someone who both confesses and leaves the sin. The second פסוק (איכה) says to lift our heart together with our hands. Raising hands in prayer is not enough unless the heart truly comes back to God. The word 'hands' also connects back to the 'violence in their hands' of נינוה.

keyTerms.meaning: And it says (introduces a second supporting פסוק)

phrases.english: As it is stated: "But whoever confesses and forsakes them shall obtain mercy,"
And it says: "Let us lift up our heart with our hands
to God in heaven."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings scriptural support for רב אדא בר אהבה's parable.
steps.raayaObject: The teaching that confession without leaving the sin does not work.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משלי 28:13 ('confesses and forsakes') and איכה 3:41 ('lift our heart with our hands').

steps.title: The prayer leader must be someone who is 'רגיל'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה about who leads the prayer on a fast day. A ברייתא says that even if an elder and a scholar is there, only a person who is 'רגיל' is sent to lead.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'They stood for prayer, and they send an elder down before the ark, etc.' The רבנן taught in a ברייתא: They stood for prayer. Even if there is an elder and a scholar there, they send down before the ark only a person who is 'רגיל' (fit and used to it).
steps.whatsHappening: The aggadah about נינוה is finished, and the גמרא goes back to the next line of the משנה. It quotes the משנה and then brings a ברייתא that adds a condition for choosing the חזן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה mentions sending a זקן (elder) to lead. The ברייתא adds that being old or wise is not enough. The leader must be 'רגיל', and the next step will explain what that means.

keyTerms.meaning: They send down before the ark, meaning they appoint someone to lead the prayer
A person who is 'used to it', the fitting kind of person to lead

steps.confusionAlert: 'רגיל' does not simply mean an experienced חזן here. רבי יהודה will explain it as someone whose life situation makes him pray with a full heart for rain.

phrases.english: They stood for prayer,
and they send down before the ark an elder, etc.
The Sages taught:
They stood for prayer,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ שָׁם זָקֵן וְחָכָם —
phrases.english: even if there is an elder and a scholar there,
they do not send down before the ark
anyone except a person who is accustomed.

steps.triggerLanguage: עָמְדוּ בִּתְפִלָּה, מוֹרִידִין לִפְנֵי הַתֵּיבָה זָקֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the aggadic discussion and goes back to explain the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even if an elder and scholar is present, only a person who is 'רגיל' is appointed to lead the fast-day prayer.

steps.title: רבי יהודה describes the right prayer leader
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה begins to describe who counts as 'רגיל': a man with children to support who cannot support them, who must work hard in the field, and whose house is empty.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: [It is] someone who has a family to support but does not have [the money], who has to work hard in the field, and whose house is empty,
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה starts explaining what kind of person the ברייתא means. His list continues in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The leader should be someone who really feels the drought. His children depend on him, his food comes from the field, and his house is empty. Such a person will pray for rain from the heart, because his family's life depends on it.

keyTerms.meaning: Burdened with dependents (a family to support)
And he does not have (the means)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that on a fast day the main quality of the חזן is a broken, sincere heart, not only age or learning.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
One who has dependents but does not have the means,
and he has toil in the field,
and his house is empty,

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: מְטוּפָּל וְאֵין לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the term 'אדם הרגיל' from the ברייתא in step 42.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'רגיל' leader is a man burdened with a family he cannot support, who works hard in the field and has an empty house, so he will pray with full intention.

steps.title: The rest of the qualities needed in the fast-day prayer leader
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה continues his list. The prayer leader must have had a clean youth, be humble, be liked by the people, have a sweet voice, know תורה, נביאים and כתובים, know מדרש, הלכות and אגדות, and know all the ברכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And his youth was proper, and he is humble, and the people like him, and he knows how to sing, and his voice is pleasant, and he is skilled at reading the תורה, the נביאים and the כתובים, and at learning מדרש, הלכות and אגדות, and he is skilled in all the ברכות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still quoting רבי יהודה's list from step 43 and now gives the rest of the qualities. These are about character, popularity, voice and learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 43 described a man whose need is real, so he prays from the heart. This step adds that his past must be clean, so no one can point to old sins, and that the people must want him, because he speaks for all of them. He also needs a good voice and broad knowledge so he can lead the long fast-day service properly.

keyTerms.meaning: His youth was proper. He had no bad name when he was young.
Accepted and liked by the people.
Musical skill, knowing how to sing the tunes.
The three areas of תורה שבעל פה: explaining פסוקים, practical laws, and stories or lessons.
Expert in all the blessings, including the extra ones said on a fast day.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'ופרקו נאה' as 'his chapter is nice.' Here פרק means a stage of life, so it refers to his youth. The point is that his past is clean.
steps.whyThisMatters: This list is used later in הלכה to describe the ideal שליח ציבור, especially for the ימים נוראים.

phrases.english: and his youth was becoming,
phrases.notes: No bad reputation from his younger years.

phrases.english: and he is humble,
and accepted by the people,
and he is familiar with melody, and his voice is pleasant,
and he is expert in reading the Torah,
the Prophets and the Writings,
and in studying midrash,
halakhot and aggadot,
and expert in all of the blessings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly continues רבי יהודה's list begun in step 43.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fast-day leader must be needy and burdened, with a clean past. He must also be humble, popular, musical, and learned in all of Torah and the ברכות.

steps.title: The Sages look at רב יצחק בר אמי as the living example
steps.stepSummary: After hearing the description, the חכמים turned their eyes toward רב יצחק בר אמי, because he had all these qualities.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים set their eyes on רב יצחק בר אמי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a short story. When the list was said, everyone looked at רב יצחק בר אמי, because he matched it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list is long and sounds almost impossible to meet. This line shows that a real person did fit it, so the description is not just an ideal. It closes the section on who should lead the fast-day prayers.

keyTerms.meaning: They set their eyes on, meaning they all looked toward him.
An אמורא who matched every quality on the list.

steps.whatToRemember: The fast-day שליח ציבור must be 'רגיל'. That means he truly feels the need, has a clean past, is humble and liked, has a pleasant voice, and is fully learned. רב יצחק בר אמי was the real-life example.

phrases.english: And the Sages turned their eyes
toward Rav Yitzḥak bar Ami.

steps.triggerLanguage: וִיהַבוּ בֵּיהּ רַבָּנַן עֵינַיְיהוּ בְּרַב יִצְחָק בַּר אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that shows a real person fitting the list from steps 43–44.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ideal fast-day leader really exists. רב יצחק בר אמי was the one the חכמים recognized as fitting the description.
